title: Tempered admission gate and standby-lease fallback for regional hotspots
author: Maya Patel
release_notes: Introduce a tempered admission gate to avoid rapid circuit flips during regional hotspots and a standby-lease fallback to preserve KV cache continuity when nodes transition. Improves tail latency stability under bursty tenant traffic. No user-facing API changes.
description: Motivation: we've seen repeated regional hotspots where rapid admit/deny churn causes circuit flips and unnecessary KV cache invalidation. This PR introduces a 'tempered admission gate' that smooths admission decisions using a short tokenized window and an explicit standby-lease fallback that keeps KV cache state available on a standby subset while avoiding full promotion unless health signals stabilize. The change targets SLO stability (p50/p95) and reduces cascading fallbacks during transients. What this PR does: 1) Adds tempered_gate component that maintains a sliding acceptance score per-route and applies hysteresis to admit/deny decisions. 2) Adds lease_manager abstraction and a standby-lease fallback implementation that keeps a small set of warm standbys with preserved KV pointers and a lightweight ownership token for fast mesh handoff. 3) Integrates admission telemetry (decision_reason, score, window) into existing tracing and metrics so rollouts can be monitored and tuned. 4) Adds unit and e2e tests that simulate regional spike, network partition, and graceful drain scenarios. Checklist: - [x] Design doc reviewed (ENG-4821) - [x] Unit tests added for tempered gate heuristics - [x] E2E test for standby lease during node promotion - [x] Metrics and tracing hooks instrumented - [x] Load testing on benchmark-lab for three spike shapes - [x] Ops runbook added to console/docs/tempered-admission.md Changes summary: see commits for stepwise refactor. Rolling out: feature gated behind runtime.config.enable_tempered_admission (false by default). Deploy plan: canary to 5% in us-west, observe acceptance_score and failover_counts for 24h before broad rollout. Backout: disable the feature gate and trigger lease_manager->evict_standbys to drop warm pointers. Note: this is a behavioral change in admission logic tuned for production SLOs; we run with default off until ops confirms telemetry stability.

notes_for_ops: Canary steps: enable runtime.config.enable_tempered_admission on 5% of serving pods in us-west, watch tempered_admission.acceptance_score_{p50,p95}, standby_fallback.promotions, and failover_counts. If promoted_standbys > 0.5% of requests for > 1h, reduce canary to 1% and investigate. If eviction oscillation observed, lower runtime.config.tempered.hysteresis_window_ms. Backout: set enable_tempered_admission=false and call tools/ops/lease_inspector.py --evict-standbys to clear warm pointers.
